group: insects: Camponotus carpenter ants (4 structures: 82-LM frontal head, 61-LM lateral head, 52-LM pronotum, 46-LM mesosoma; 634 specimens across minor/media/major castes and 43 species)

data.landmarks: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18807285 ('Camponotus ecomorphospace: Morphological evolution mediated by nesting adaptation in South American carpenter ants', 2026/2027); 634 specimens across 43 species (42 with paired minor 'w' and major 's' castes, 41 on the calibrated phylogeny) digitized on 4 homologous structures: Head Frontal View (82 2D landmarks), Head Lateral View (61 2D landmarks), Pronotum Dorsal View (52 2D landmarks), and Mesosoma Lateral Profile (46 2D landmarks).
data.phylogeny: Calibrated Camponotus phylogeny `tree_CAM.tre` from the same deposit (`camponotus_bodyplan2.zip`), pruned to unique species tips (41 matched species after standardizing `Dendromyrmex` -> `dendromyrmex`, `bonariensis_nr` -> `bonariensis`, `propinquellus_nr` -> `propinquus`, `scipio_nr` -> `scipio`, `ag_br02` -> `sp02`, `ag_br04` -> `sp04`; deduplicating duplicate tip entries in `tree_CAM.tre` for `blandus`, `excisus`, and `senex`).
data.status: landmark data previously used for within-species minor->major 8p nonlinear caste allometry (`thompson/run_antscan_caste_allometry_tests.py`); never tested with the 7-D linearized Thompson tangent basis (`thompson_mode_basis`), never compared caste vs between-species variance in Thompson-7 across the 4 structures, and never run through the leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction engine on `tree_CAM.tre`. Hypotheses A1-A8 registered before running.

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Ants provide a within-group developmental control that neither fish nor hornet/bee wings have: the exact same 4 anatomical structures (frontal head, lateral head, pronotum, mesosoma) undergo BOTH within-species developmental polyphenism (minor worker -> media -> major soldier caste allometry) AND between-species macroevolutionary radiation across nesting syndromes (twig, ground, rotten wood). If Thompson's 7 global coordinate modes describe continuous growth-field gradients (such as juvenile-hormone / insulin-signaling head-capsule expansion in soldier ants), then within-species minor -> major caste shifts should be much more Thompsonian than between-species evolutionary divergence on the same landmarks, and the frontal head capsule (where soldier allometry acts) should be far more Thompsonian in caste polyphenism than in interspecific divergence.

hypotheses.statement: Within-species minor ('w') -> major ('s') caste vectors are MORE Thompsonian than between-species species-mean divergence: pooled across the 42 dimorphic species on the 82-landmark frontal head, the 7 a-priori Thompson modes capture a larger share of within-species minor->major caste variance than of between-species species-mean variance (and > 50% of caste variance).
hypotheses.reasoning: Soldier head development is driven by a single continuous imaginal-disc growth gradient (occipital fan expansion + cordate vertex elevation), whereas interspecific divergence across nesting syndromes modifies local clypeal, mandibular, and eye proportions.

hypotheses.statement: Across all 4 structures (frontal head 82 LM, lateral head 61 LM, pronotum 52 LM, mesosoma 46 LM), within-species minor->major caste vectors have a higher Thompson-7 variance share than between-species divergence in at least 3 of the 4 structures.
hypotheses.reasoning: Ontogenetic caste polyphenism is a systemic endocrine growth scaling across the body wall, whereas interspecific adaptation to twig vs ground nesting introduces local modular changes.

hypotheses.statement: Between-species frontal-head shape (82 LMs, 41 tree species) is MORE Thompsonian than insect wing venation: Thompson-7 captures > 0.422 (the bee-wing benchmark) of between-species variance in species-mean frontal heads.
hypotheses.reasoning: Unlike wing vein intersections (which shift locally in the wing interior), the 82 frontal-head landmarks trace a continuous head-capsule outline + eye/clypeus geometry where width-to-length aspect and posterior fan dominate.

hypotheses.statement: Phylogenetic signal on `tree_CAM.tre`: Pagel's lambda (or BM/OU/EB over White Noise by AICc) is non-zero (lambda > 0.3, best model != White Noise) in Thompson-7 scores across all 4 structures.
hypotheses.reasoning: The dataset authors reported moderate phylogenetic signal alongside ecological nesting convergence (ENS).

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction beats the consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.95, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.05) in at least 2 of the 4 structures.
hypotheses.reasoning: With 41 species on a resolved calibrated tree (unlike the polytomous Open Tree in Vespa), closely related Camponotus species share subgeneric body plans, though strong ecomorphic convergence across nesting habits caps the gain.

hypotheses.statement: Thompson-7 captures at least 50% of the full-space leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction gain (relative to consensus) on the frontal head (82 LMs), matching or exceeding fish bodies (55.5%).
hypotheses.reasoning: If phylogenetic conservatism in Camponotus head shape lies primarily in overall head elongation/fanning, Thompson-7 will carry most of the tree-predictable signal.

hypotheses.statement: Developmental channelling (G_caste vs R_species): the principal axis of within-species minor->major caste divergence aligns more strongly with the principal axis of between-species macroevolutionary divergence inside the 7-D Thompson subspace than in the orthogonal non-Thompson modular residual subspace (|cos theta|_T7 > |cos theta|_res) across at least 3 of the 4 structures.
hypotheses.reasoning: Extends Schluter's (1996) line-of-least-resistance test from fish genera to ant caste polyphenism: macroevolutionary radiation reuses the global Thompsonian caste-allometry highway while diverging orthogonally in local modular traits.

hypotheses.statement: Where the global grid fails on the 82-LM frontal head: between-species unexplained residual fraction after Thompson-7 is HIGHER on interior/anterior sensory-oral landmarks (mandibles, clypeus, frontal carinae, eyes: landmarks closest to the centroid/anterior oral pole) than on the outer lateral/occipital head-capsule contour.
hypotheses.reasoning: The outer head capsule deforms as a smooth continuous shell under Thompson's modes, whereas interior/oral landmarks (eyes, antennal insertions, clypeal margin) shift locally across nesting guilds.

protocol.species_set: All 43 species in `camponotus_morphometric2.zip` for variance/caste tests (42 with both 'w' minor and 's' major workers); the 41 species present on `tree_CAM.tre` for phylogenetic signal and leave-one-species-out prediction.
protocol.shape_space: For each structure (headFV 82 LM, headLV 61 LM, pronotum 52 LM, mesosoma 46 LM): GPA across all specimens -> species means (and species-by-caste means) -> OPA onto consensus M0; Thompson-7 basis = `thompson_mode_basis(M0)` from `thompson/run_phylogenetic_prediction_engine.py`.
protocol.process_models: fit_models (WN, BM, lambda, OU, EB; AICc) on `tree_CAM.tre` in Thompson-7 and full PCA-95% spaces.
protocol.validation: Leave-one-species-out conditional Gaussian prediction (`predict()`) across the 41 tree species; paired one-sided Wilcoxon tests on per-species Procrustes RMS.
protocol.no_tuning: All 8 hypotheses, thresholds, and species-name mappings are locked in this JSON before writing or running `camponotus_ants.py`.
